changes: confcheck --fix --write now also fixes the file permissions it warns about (chmod 600 on config files, backups and the TLS key, go-w on config directories), for files you own; ones needing sudo or a chown are still left to you. --fix alone previews them

Config wizard: tools/makeconf.py (also sekurircd --makeconf) asks a few questions and writes a complete sekurircd.toml and, for NickServ + ChanServ, a matching services.toml. Passwords are hashed with scrypt, files are written 0600, existing ones are backed up, and both daemons' --check must accept the result. With the Protection bundle on it also writes protection.toml (connection caps, flood guard, EFnet DNSBL, spam protection, proxy scanner). It can make a self-signed certificate too. The same wizard is on the website (docs/wizard.html), running in the browser

Config templates rewritten to be easier to read: grouped by category with short headers, shorter comments, and the stale ones fixed (version, cloak format, ChanServ paths, REHASH). Newly documented: [server] sid, [[operators]] privileges and modes, [[classes]] sendq_max, [links] max_line_length. Every setting and default is unchanged
services.template.toml: removed a duplicated [link] header that made a straight copy of the template invalid TOML
ChanServ: an ACCESS entry by account (=account) now gives its mode when the user logs in to NickServ after joining the channel. Before, the mode only came on join, so identifying late meant a /cycle

Oper modes are configurable, like UnrealIRCd's modes-on-oper and Solanum's oper_umodes: [security] oper_modes (default "+osw") sets what every /OPER gets, and a login's own modes = "..." in [[operators]] replaces it (e.g. "+oswW" for a netadmin who wants WHOIS notices). o is always given; allowed on top are iwdTsBgZpIRD and the oper-only H, q and W. An unknown letter fails the config load. The MODE line after /OPER now lists only the modes that were actually added

Users who reach us over TLS through a web gateway or reverse proxy now get +z too, so they can join +z (TLS-only) channels: a WEBIRC with the IRCv3 "secure" option, and a WebSocket from a trusted_proxies address whose X-Forwarded-Proto is https at every hop. Direct TLS and wss connections already had it

REHASH now reports what it did. The oper gets 382 with the config path, then one "*** Rehash:" NOTICE per item: the config and Protection bundle files, which sections changed (or "no setting changed"), the MOTD/oper MOTD/rules files with their line counts, the spam-filter file with its rule count, any listener rebinds, and the TLS certificate reload. Other opers get a "<nick> is rehashing server config file" snotice

The MOTD, oper MOTD, rules and spam filters are yours, not git's: the repo now ships config/ircd.template.motd, oper.template.motd, ircd.template.rules and spamfilters.template.conf, and the live ircd.motd/oper.motd/ircd.rules/spamfilters.conf are untracked (.gitignore). The ircd creates a missing one from its template at start and on REHASH and never touches an existing one. Upgrading keeps your edited files as they are; a file you never edited is recreated from the new template. make install no longer overwrites an installed spamfilters.conf (it lost SPAMFILTER ADD rules on every reinstall)

MODE #chan from outside a keyed channel lost every argument after the hidden key: "+ntkl *" came back without the limit. Only the key is replaced with "*" now ("+ntkl * 5"). The 221 sent at connect also had a buffer too small for every user mode at once

Bans typed as a bare host or user@host now work. "+b 1.2.3.4", "+b *.example.com" and "+b baduser@host" used to be stored as-is and matched only against the nick, so they banned nobody. Masks are now stored in canonical form, as UnrealIRCd does it ("*!*@1.2.3.4", "*!baduser@host", "bob!*@*"), and -b finds them again
UnrealIRCd 6 named extbans are accepted: ~account:, ~quiet: or ~q:, ~realname:, ~channel: or ~c: are stored as our ~a:, ~m:, ~r: and ~j:
A MODE change that changes nothing (+n on a +n channel, -k with no key, +i when already invisible) is no longer broadcast, so client scripts that re-send modes stop flooding the channel

User modes now use UnrealIRCd's letters: +d is deaf (channel messages are not delivered to you, private ones still are) and +T drops CTCP sent to you, which +d used to do. If your [security] default_user_modes has a d, change it to T
New channel mode +K disables /KNOCK (480). New extban ~n:<mask> (UnrealIRCd's ~nickchange:) stops matching users from changing nick in the channel; voice and up are exempt
[security] default_user_modes accepted B and g but never applied them; it now does

The TLS user mode is now +z, as in UnrealIRCd, and +Z means private messages only to and from TLS users (531 otherwise; opers and services still get through). Linked servers still exchange it under the old letters, so a mixed-version network keeps working

+f takes UnrealIRCd's form too: [<n><type>[#<action>[<mins>]],...]:<secs>, with types c (CTCP), j (joins), k (knocks), m (messages), n (nick changes) and t (lines per user, kick or #b kick-ban). When a limit is passed the server sets the action mode (+C, +i, +K, +m, +N, or the alternative given) and removes it again after <mins> if a number is given. The plain <lines>:<secs> form still works
Timed bans: ~t:<minutes>:<mask> (or ~time:) on +b, +e or +I is removed by the server once the time is up, and works around any other mask, e.g. ~t:30:~m:*!*@host for a 30-minute quiet
New extban ~S:<fingerprint> (or ~certfp:) matches the SHA-256 fingerprint of a user's TLS client certificate
Ban, exception and invite-exception lists (367/348/346) now show who set each entry and when, as other ircds do

User mode +x: on by default under host_masking. -x shows your real host and +x cloaks it again (396 tells you the new host; CHGHOST goes to channel-mates). +x also works with host_masking off. Bans still match the real host and IP
User mode +W (opers only): a server notice whenever someone does a /WHOIS on you, from any server on the network
Forward bans: ~f:#chan:<mask> (or ~forward:) sends a matching user's JOIN to #chan instead of refusing it with 474
+f takes the r type too: the same line repeated <n> times by one user kicks them (#b kick-bans, #d just drops the line)

ChanServ takeover protection, as on Anope. ChanServ remembers each registered channel's TS. A channel recreated since it last saw it (on another server, during a netsplit, or while services were down) is reset: default modes, no +k/+i/+l/redirect, empty ban/exception/invite lists, then +r, MLOCK and a locked topic back. Anyone holding ops who isn't the founder, identified or on the access list at a level covering the rank loses them (SECUREOPS no longer needed for this). A channel with the TS it already knows, such as one a relinking server brings back, is left alone. On relink, ChanServ sweeps every registered channel, giving ACCESS modes and kicking AKICK/RESTRICTED members who joined meanwhile. ACCESS and AKICK work on JOIN in every registered channel, not only GUARDed ones. ChanServ can't be kicked or deopped (484). SECUREOPS checks each +o against the access level (a v entry no longer covers @). SJOIN with a TS of 0 or less no longer wins every channel. Mode changes that change nothing are no longer echoed

Fix (linked servers): a user joining a channel with members on another server also got that server's own topic and NAMES replies (331/332/353/366), once per remote server, and again when a server relinked. Only the user's own server answers a JOIN now

Fix: draft/multiline messages lost their line breaks and everything past 419 bytes in CHATHISTORY (they were stored as one flattened line, although up to 4096 bytes are accepted). History keeps the whole batch: clients with draft/multiline get it back as a multiline batch inside the chathistory batch, others as one message per line, as live
Fix: spam filters only checked the first 419 bytes of a multiline batch; the whole text is checked now

Fix: the user part was shown two ways. JOIN/PRIVMSG prefixes said ~user (ident not confirmed) while 001, WHOIS (311), WHO (352/354 u), NAMES with userhost-in-names (353), WHOWAS (314), USERHOST/USERIP (302), WATCH (604/600) and CHGHOST said user, so a ban copied from WHOIS (*!user@host) didn't match. All of them show the ~ now. ChanServ's NOTICEs no longer carry a ~ its MODE lines don't have. A CHGIDENT on a user on another server now reaches every server as a confirmed ident
labeled-response: REGISTER (draft/account-registration) answered ACK at once and sent REGISTER SUCCESS/FAIL unlabeled when services replied; the reply now carries the label and no ACK is sent
CHATHISTORY and MARKREAD without their capability (or with history off) answer FAIL ... INVALID instead of nothing
LIST: 321 is "321 nick Channel :Users  Name" (it was one trailing parameter)
[channels] default_modes defaults to "nt" when the key is missing, as the template says (it was empty, so channels took external messages)

draft/multiline across linked servers: a batch sent on one server reached users on the others as one flattened line cut at 419 bytes, and was stored that way in their CHATHISTORY. Its lines now travel with it (a new MLINE link line just before the message), so users on every server get the same multiline batch, or one message per line without the cap, and every server's history keeps it whole. Servers older than 1.3.2 ignore MLINE and still deliver the flattened message, so mixed networks keep working (a pre-1.3.2 server in the middle of a path flattens what passes through it)

tools/upgrade.py: when upstream rewrote its history (same code, new commit hashes) it said "diverged" and could not upgrade; it now says "same code as <commit> (upstream history was rewritten)" and moves the checkout onto upstream's history, keeping local edits. It also tells you when what runs isn't the checkout yet (bin/sekurircd older than the source, or a daemon started before the last build) and offers to rebuild and restart it. The menu's default is never an option older than your checkout (it was always [1], the latest release, even when that was a downgrade)

IRCv3: draft/event-playback. CHATHISTORY replays joins, parts, quits, kicks, mode and topic changes, nick changes and TAGMSG reactions (+draft/react, +draft/reply; never +typing) to clients that ask for it; other clients still get only messages, and their limits and references count only messages. [messages] history_events = false keeps messages only
IRCv3: draft/extended-isupport. The ISUPPORT command sends the 005 list on demand, also before registration, and with batch every 005 list comes in a draft/isupport batch
IRCv3: netsplit and netjoin batches. The quits of a split and the joins of a relink each come in one batch, so clients can fold them

IRCv3 UTF8ONLY: lines that aren't valid UTF-8 are refused with FAIL <command> INVALID_UTF8 and never relayed. On by default; [messages] utf8_only = false turns it off for networks with legacy-charset users
IRCv3: draft/ICON ([server] icon) and CLIENTTAGDENY ([messages] client_tag_deny) in 005; a +draft/channel-context tag is only relayed when it names a channel the sender is on
SASL re-authentication: a logged-in client may run SASL again to switch accounts (it got 907 before); a failed attempt keeps the current login

Event loop: kqueue (macOS/BSD) or epoll (Linux) instead of poll(), with a poll() fallback elsewhere. Each connection's interest is registered once and changed only when it changes, so a wakeup costs the number of busy connections instead of the number of connections; idle clients no longer slow everyone else down

REDACT (draft/message-redaction): take back a message still in history. Your own, or anyone's in a channel you operate (IRC operators too). It is removed from CHATHISTORY on every server, and clients with the cap hide it
PRIVMSG and NOTICE take up to 4 comma-separated targets (TARGMAX=PRIVMSG:4,NOTICE:4); each target counts against the flood limit and the spam limits like a separate message
Read markers take only the memory their key needs (they reserved 200 bytes each)

Fix: renaming a channel onto the name of a registered but empty channel walked past ChanServ, so the renamer kept op and the channel got no +r, MLOCK or SECUREOPS. A rename is now checked by services like a channel created by JOIN
Fix: spam filters skipped messages to ~#chan and &#chan (owners/admins only), treating them as private messages
Read markers (draft/read-marker) follow a channel RENAME; CHGIDENT re-checks SHUNs against the new ident
WHOIS: the 311 reply now includes the standard "*" field before the realname; strict clients (iSekur) failed to parse it without it

Spam filters: new hide and shun actions. hide drops a matching message silently: the sender gets no notice, and echo-message clients see it as sent. shun does the same and also SHUNs the sender's IP network-wide for the rule's duration. Opers are still notified
Linked servers: numeric replies now reach users on other servers. KNOCK reaches chanops on every server (it used to reach only those on the knocker's server)
WHOIS <nick> <nick> is answered by the user's own server, so idle time shows across links; MOTD, ADMIN, INFO, VERSION and TIME take a server name to ask that server
SHUN/UNSHUN are network-wide like GLINE (also sent to servers that link later); a SHUN set on one server used to do nothing to users on the others

KILL of a user on another server: the victim now gets the KILL line, and the quit reason names the oper (Killed (oper (reason))) the way a local KILL does; that server's opers get the 'Received KILL' notice
UNGLINE coming over a link removed the first line of any type with that mask, possibly a local K- or Z-line instead of the G-line. It now removes only the G-line
SQUERY to a service linked to another server reaches it (it used to be dropped silently)
Netsplits: a topic changed on one side during a split now survives the relink (the newer topic wins; it used to revert to the older one)
A leaf that dropped a dead link (ping timeout) waits until it is torn down before redialing, instead of refusing its own first reconnect and making the hub see an extra link up/down

IPv6 (opt-in): [server] ipv6 = true gives every listener (clients, TLS, WebSocket, server links) an IPv6 socket next to its IPv4 one. Off by default, so an upgrade changes nothing; separate IPv6-only sockets keep IPv4 clients and existing bans exactly as they were. IPv6 clients show as e.g. 2001:db8::5 (::1 as 0::1, since an IRC parameter can't start with ':'); reverse DNS, ident, DNSBL and link dialing work over IPv6; the proxy scanner stays IPv4-only

CIDR masks: K/G/Z-lines and E-lines, allowed_ips, oper hosts, WEBIRC/class/proxy hosts and protection exemptions take CIDR as well as globs (2001:db8::/32, 203.0.113.0/24). Per-IP limits, connect-flood auto-bans and host cloaks count an IPv6 client by its /64 (ipv6_limit_prefix), so rotating addresses inside it gets around none of them
Fix: every WEBIRC or X-Forwarded-For connection leaked one slot of the gateway's per-IP count, so a busy web chat gateway was eventually refused with "Too many connections from your host"

Link wizard: tools/linkmgmt.py add, edit and del now write this server's side of a link themselves: the [[links.peers]] block and any [links] changes, after showing the diff and asking. A private backup is kept, the ircd's own --check validates the result and a refused change is restored; then it rehashes the running ircd or says a restart is needed. The other server's side is still printed to paste there, and can be saved to a private file to copy over. --dry-run keeps the print-only behaviour
Testing: 139 end-to-end integration tests (IPv6 clients, CIDR bans, per-/64 limits, IPv6 links, rehash on/off, the gateway count fix)

Server links: pin each other's TLS certificate with fingerprint = "sha256:..." in [[links.peers]]. Self-signed certificates work without tls_insecure_skip_verify, a server that doesn't show the pinned certificate is refused before any password is sent or checked, and with a fingerprint the password is optional, so neither side has to keep a plain-text secret. The dialing server now presents its own [tls] certificate, and the accepting one asks for it
Server links: turning on [links] tls no longer cuts off the services daemon, which doesn't speak TLS: plain links are still accepted from 127.0.0.1, and only TLS from anywhere else

Passwords: tools/confcheck.py --fix --write turns plain-text passwords into scrypt password_hash lines (operators, die/restart, link peers the server only accepts from); the same passwords keep working. The ircd logs a reminder at start and on /REHASH while any are left

File permissions: confcheck warns about configs, the TLS key, account and ChanServ stores and --fix backups that other local users can read or change, with the exact chmod/chown for each case; --fix backups are now private (0600)
Tools: tools/linkmgmt.py fingerprint prints this server's certificate fingerprint, test HOST PORT --tls shows the other server's, and the add/edit wizard offers pinning
Testing: 132 end-to-end integration tests (pinned TLS links, wrong pins on either side, services over loopback)

Services: NickServ now runs in the services daemon next to ChanServ (bin/services, services 1.4.0) instead of inside every ircd. One account database for the whole network: every server relays SASL (PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, EXTERNAL), REGISTER and PASS logins to it, so accounts can no longer diverge in a netsplit. Nick enforcement, GHOST and REGAIN work across servers; services admins are accounts listed in [nickserv] admins. While services are down, SASL is not offered and existing logins stay logged in

Upgrade: nothing to convert -- NickServ uses the existing config/accounts.json in place (the pre-upgrade file is kept as accounts.json.bak1); the old [accounts] section is ignored with a warning. Account and ChanServ stores keep rotating backups and never start empty over a corrupt file (they load the newest good backup or refuse to start)

Tools: ./sekurircd start|stop|restart|status manages the ircd and services (and retires an old standalone ChanServ); systemd services.service replaces chanserv.service and follows sekurircd.service; upgrade.py, make install, confcheck and the config backup handle the switch

Server linking: a server joining a large network no longer loses part of the burst (the link send queue was a fixed 32 KB); TLS links no longer stall the burst until the next PING; ChanServ's ops and UNBAN reach every server; SAJOIN/SAPART/SANICK/CHGHOST/CHGIDENT work on users of other servers; servers exchange their link protocol and version at handshake (compatible versions are announced to opers, incompatible ones refused)
Testing: 127 end-to-end integration tests (multi-server bursts, TLS links, services across servers, upgrade of old data)

NickServ: RESETPASS (emailed one-time code to the verified address, then a new password), REGAIN (take your nick back in one step), oper SUSPEND/UNSUSPEND, FDROP and SASET PASSWORD behind a new "accounts" oper privilege (suspensions replicate across linked servers and log the account out everywhere); /WHOIS NickServ answers as a network service; /NS, /NICKSERV, /CS and /CHANSERV shorthands. email_command now gets "verify" or "reset" as a fifth argument
Lower memory use: per-client lists allocated on demand, compact chat history, heap-allocated tables
Channel flood (+f) no longer counts TAGMSG, so typing indicators can't get anyone kicked

Web chat v2 (shared with www.sekurnet.org/chat/): home-screen app, tabs with close buttons, nick menu and colors, read markers, event icons, commands, /list dialog, typing indicators, desktop notifications, away/account markers, paste guard, text size and a hideable user list; new web chat docs page

Tools: tools/confcheck.py config validator (and sekurircd/chanserv --check; upgrade.py won't restart on a bad config), warns on a [server] name without a dot; upgrade.py can install systemd user units for clone installs
#server-debug: cleaner relay format, less connection noise
Testing: 115 end-to-end integration tests (5 new NickServ tests)
Fix: registered channels now get +r, MLOCK and GUARD back when they are recreated after dying or after a restart (services only restored them for channels that already existed when they linked)

Security: with SECUREOPS on, ChanServ strips ops/voice from anyone with no claim to them when a registered channel is recreated, and when services reconnect (channels recreated while services were down no longer keep their creator as op); new registrations have SECUREOPS on by default
Testing: 101 end-to-end integration tests

Security: fixed a use-after-free when a netsplit removed a chain of three or more servers, and IP spoofing through a WebSocket reverse proxy (X-Forwarded-For is now read right-to-left, skipping trusted proxies, instead of trusting the client-supplied leftmost entry)

Client compatibility: usernames like john.doe (the OS login irssi, WeeChat and HexChat send) are cleaned up instead of disconnecting the client; a full-length CAP REQ (gamja, Kiwi, Halloy) is no longer refused; MONITOR lists are split across lines instead of truncated; labeled responses no longer double-tag lines inside CHATHISTORY/multiline batches; STATUSMSG (@#chan) is echoed to echo-message clients; NAMES lines always fit in 512 bytes
New: WHO <mask> (nick, user, host, server, realname; 'o' for opers only), PASS account:password login for clients without SASL, and JOIN 0
Privacy: +i users no longer appear in WHO masks or in WHO #channel for people outside the channel

Fixes: RENAME keeps the channel's chat history; cap-notify sends correct SASL values (EXTERNAL when available, bare names to pre-302 clients); read markers and STATS m counters are bounded correctly; web chat nick fallback can no longer stall registration
Testing: 98 end-to-end integration tests (10 new client-compatibility tests)

Multi-server networking: SekurIRCd servers now link into a tree and share users, channels, modes, topics, bans, messages, away/account/host state and G-lines, with TS-based channel merging, nick-collision resolution, netsplit QUITs, /MAP, /LINKS, /SQUIT (also remote), /CONNECT, KILL/WALLOPS/GLOBOPS across servers and ChanServ serving users on any server. links.mode "both" with several [[links.peers]] and links.autoconnect
Accounts are replicated between linked servers (register, password, email, grouped nicks, drop; sent in the burst, last writer wins)

IRCv3: CAP 302/cap-notify, msgid, TAGMSG, batch, labeled-response, chathistory (server-level store with optional persistence and DM history), draft/multiline, draft/read-marker, draft/channel-rename, draft/no-implicit-names, draft/pre-away, extended-monitor, SASL SCRAM-SHA-256

Channel modes +f, +j, +L, +D, +u, +G, +q/+a ranks (~ and &); extbans ~r, ~z, ~j; caller-ID (+g/ACCEPT); connection classes; WEBIRC; PROXY protocol v1/v2; WebSocket (ws/wss) listener; oper privilege classes, SHUN, ELINE, GLOBOPS, SANICK, CHGIDENT, TESTLINE, LOCOPS, USERIP

NickServ: SET PASSWORD, DROP, LOGOUT, INFO, SET EMAIL/VERIFY, GROUP/UNGROUP, GHOST and nick enforcement. ChanServ: account-based founder, SECUREOPS, RESTRICTED, PRIVATE, LIST, extended MLOCK, owner/admin ranks

Hardening from the 2026-10 audit (stale worker results, link allowed_ips, +P abuse, NOTICE auto-replies, ISUPPORT/protocol fixes, link/worker robustness) and rehash now rebinds listeners and reloads the TLS certificate
Testing: 88-test end-to-end integration suite (make itest, including 3-server networks), clean under ASan/UBSan, plus a parser fuzz harness (make fuzz)

Security audit: fixed a TLS handshake busy-loop DoS, umode +q (unkickable) being settable by any user instead of opers only, a proxy-scanner flood/cap-limit bypass, and hostname K/G-lines and channel bans that silently never matched (rDNS result and bans now check the real host/IP, not just a possibly-cloaked displayed one)
Security: new per-IP throttle on SASL/NickServ IDENTIFY, a timing-safe decoy for unknown accounts, and a fix for a second login attempt applying its result to the wrong pending account
Security: /REGISTER's instant self-service account creation no longer grants full spam-check exemption immediately; accounts.json/klines.json are now written 0600 with fsync-before-rename
Bugfix: use-after-free on self-KICK/SAPART, case-only nick changes never being announced, and SAJOIN/auto_join handing out ops on a channel it didn't actually create

ChanServ: SUCCESSOR CLAIM now checks a claimant's real identity over the link instead of the (possibly cloaked) PRIVMSG sender host, so a hostmask or "=account" successor actually works; identified-founder state now expires and is cleared on DROP/reconnect instead of occasionally sticking forever and permanently blocking a legitimate CLAIM; AKICK now also sets a ban; several crash/data-loss fixes in the JSON store
New channel modes +R (registered-only join), +O (oper-only join), +M (registered/voice+ only speak), +c (reject colour/formatting outright)
New quiet extban m:/~m: (blocks speaking, not joining); ~a: alias for the existing a:account extban; /LIST now matches a #-prefixed pattern and a leading ! negates
New ChanServ commands: OP/DEOP/VOICE/DEVOICE/HALFOP/DEHALFOP, INVITE, UNBAN, KICK, TOPIC
New IRCv3 STS support ([tls] sts_duration)

Performance: O(1) worker-result lookup (was O(n) per result, O(n^2) across a connect burst) and a send buffer that shrinks back down after a large burst instead of staying at its peak size for the connection's life

New Protection bundle: an optional, one-file abuse-protection layer (config/protection.toml, template in config/protection.template.toml) that groups DNSBL blacklists, the new proxy scanner, connection limits, the connect-flood throttle, the per-client flood guard and spam protection. Leave the file out and nothing changes

Active open-proxy scanner ([scanner], off by default): on connect the server tries HTTP CONNECT, HTTP POST, SOCKS4 and SOCKS5 back through the client's own address to its own public address; a working relay bans the address and drops everyone connected from it. Runs in the background on non-blocking sockets in the main loop, with a per-probe timeout, a concurrency cap and an optional negative cache

DNSBL blacklists moved into the bundle ([blacklist]) and gained per-zone reply rules: exact or bitmask reply codes, ban_unknown, and a per-zone ban reason with %i/%t/%r placeholders. The old [dnsbl] section keeps working and logs a deprecation warning

Connection caps, the connect-flood throttle, the flood guard and [spam] can now live in the bundle file ([connection], [flood], [spam]); where the bundle sets a key it overrides sekurircd.toml, and the old keys still work
[exempt] lists IP globs that are never DNSBL-checked or scanned; connections a scan relays back to the server are exempt from the connect-flood throttle and per-IP cap
New oper command /PROTECT shows the bundle's state and counters; /PROTECT SCAN <ip> scans an address on demand. /VERSION shows a P flag for the scanner
Bundle activity is logged with the protection/dnsbl tags and relayed into your debug channel: bans, a startup/REHASH summary and the periodic stats line now include proxy-scanner counters
A DNSBL hit now also disconnects every other connection from that address; the server sends the standard NOTICE AUTH "*** Looking up your hostname" line on connect
Docs: new Protection bundle page and config template
Security: fixed a remotely-triggerable stack buffer overflow in channel MODE handling, reachable by any channel operator
Security: ident/rDNS/DNSBL lookups are now bounded by their configured timeouts (dnsbl.timeout and rdns_timeout were previously ignored) and can no longer stall the worker pool
Security: bans, /SILENCE and ChanServ ACCESS/AKICK now match identd-confirmed users correctly; a mask written the way WHOIS displays a user finally bites
KLINE/GLINE now match host and user@host masks, not just IPs; ZLINE stays IP-only for connect-time bans
Security: constant-time password comparison for OPER/DIE/RESTART and server links; hardened build flags (stack protector, FORTIFY_SOURCE, RELRO/BIND_NOW on Linux)
INVITE can no longer be used to send arbitrary text around /SILENCE, +D and +R
Fixed an out-of-descriptors condition that pegged a CPU core, and a lost auth result that permanently wedged a connection's ability to log in
/REGISTER is rate-limited and the account store is capped ([accounts] max_accounts)
Config validation no longer overflows on a bad host_masking_token_bytes; max_params, max_nick_length and max_message_length are range-checked
Performance: O(1) per-IP connection counting, deduplicated and batched K-line writes, debounced ChanServ store writes
A leaf server reconnect no longer freezes the event loop for the OS connect timeout
SASL EXTERNAL: log in with a TLS client certificate, bound with /CERT ADD
Z-lines (ZLINE/UNZLINE), /WATCH, and STATS k/g/z/l
Per-IP connect-flood throttle that auto-bans scanners
Server-notice (+s) alerts for OPER, failed OPER, KILL, links, and SA*/SETHOST overrides
Optional oper host masking on /OPER, human-friendly ban expiry and uptime
Rootless systemd user units, make install/uninstall, and a start/stop/status wrapper script
Hardened server-link listener; random RPL_YOURID
New /RULES command backed by config/ircd.rules, and an operator MOTD (config/oper.motd) sent on /OPER and via /OPERMOTD; both reload on /REHASH
New [messages] keys: oper_motd and rules; templates for both files are included

New spam protection module ([spam], off by default): regex content filters for PRIVMSG/NOTICE (users and channels) plus AWAY, QUIT, PART and TOPIC text; a new-connection restriction on PMs; and recipient/repeat limits that catch bots messaging many targets
Filters live in config/spamfilters.conf (an example file is included) with actions block, warn, kill and zline; filters_enabled turns the file off without touching the rest
New /SPAMFILTER LIST|ADD|DEL oper command edits the filters file live; regexes are validated (no backreferences, no empty matches); rules reload on /REHASH
Opers with +s get a notice for every spam action, and services, opers and identified accounts are exempt by default

/VERSION is now ircu/solanum-style: SekurIRCd-<version>(<date>-<commit>) plus feature flags and the full 005 ISUPPORT list; WHOX and MAXCHANNELS are now advertised, and 004 carries the same build string

Accounts: IRCv3 draft/account-registration (REGISTER <account|*> <email|*> <password>) and a built-in NickServ (REGISTER / IDENTIFY) alongside /REGISTER and SASL; registering while already logged in is now refused
User mode +B marks a client as a bot (IRCv3 bot mode): 335 in WHOIS, B in WHO flags, @bot message tag, BOT=B in 005
Periodic stats server notice for opers
ChanServ bug fixes
README rewritten as a standalone project doc
Fixed crashes, security holes and performance stalls; wired up previously dead config options
New channel and user modes: +P +C +T +S +V +Q +N
Fixed the Linux build (glibc POSIX gating) and added a TLS connect notice
Expanded ChanServ HELP; fixed OPER re-auth and TOPICLOCK sync; WHOX support
Initial release of the C port
